Risk Burndown Across Submission Milestones

Source: R/risk_trend.R
risk_trend.Rd

Summarizes a sequence of risk registers, one per submission milestone, into a tidy burndown tibble. Where compare_risk_registers() and risk_reduction_summary() tell the before/after story of a single mitigation step, risk_trend() tracks the whole trajectory, so a programme can show reviewers that risk is falling milestone over milestone rather than at a single point in time.

Usage

risk_trend(registers, config = risk_config_default())

Arguments

registers

A named (or otherwise ordered) list of risk_register objects from create_risk_register(), one per milestone, earliest first.

config

A risk_config from risk_config_default(). Reserved for configurable classification; the registers' stored levels are used as-is.

Value

A tibble of class "risk_trend" with one row per milestone and the columns milestone, milestone_index, n_risks, total_rpn, mean_rpn, and n_open_critical.

Details

The registers are treated as an ordered sequence: the list order is the milestone order (earliest first). Names, when supplied, are used as milestone labels; an unnamed or blank entry falls back to milestone_<n>. Each register keeps its own already-computed rpn and risk_level (from create_risk_register() / classify_rpn()), so no scoring is recomputed here. The open-critical count is the number of risks whose level is "critical" and whose status is "open"; an empty register contributes a total and mean RPN of 0.

See also

plot_risk_trend() for the optional ggplot burndown, risk_reduction_summary() for a pairwise before/after summary.

Examples

m1 <- create_risk_register(data.frame(
  risk_id       = c("R001", "R002", "R003"),
  description   = c("Missing vars", "Bad derivation", "Define gap"),
  probability   = c(4, 5, 2),
  impact        = c(5, 5, 3),
  detectability = c(4, 4, 4)
))
m2 <- apply_mitigations(
  m1, data.frame(risk_id = c("R001", "R002"), probability = c(2, 2))
)
m3 <- apply_mitigations(
  m2, data.frame(risk_id = "R003", detectability = 1)
)
risk_trend(list(baseline = m1, interim = m2, final = m3))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   milestone milestone_index n_risks total_rpn mean_rpn n_open_critical
#> * <chr>               <int>   <int>     <dbl>    <dbl>           <int>
#> 1 baseline                1       3       204     68                 2
#> 2 interim                 2       3       104     34.7               0
#> 3 final                   3       3        86     28.7               0
